heading: How the atlas works.
Signals and uncertainty are displayed separately from verified legislative actions.
about.description: How Texas Bill Atlas reads the official record, tags bills and shows hearing progress and author prominence.
about.html:
EXPLAINABLE SIGNALS

Verified facts first. Forecasts second.

A filed bill is not a viable bill by default. Hearing progress, author prominence, policy impact, and predicted enactment are separate dimensions. No numeric forecast appears without a measured historical basis and a stated confidence level.

What is affected

Bills can carry many policy tags, legal effects, affected populations, local-government layers, and agencies. A tag can be explicitly supported or an inference, and we show that distinction.

Who filed it

Author influence is based on independently verified roles: chamber leadership, committee chairmanship, relevant committee seats, and legislative tenure. We do not assign prominence just for party or media attention.

Chance of a hearing

The atlas shows the strongest hearing signal supported by the record. A referral alone does not guarantee a hearing.

Likelihood of passage

Passage requires a separate model: committee action, chamber calendars and votes, companion progress, cross-chamber support, deadlines, and executive position. No passage probabilities are currently claimed.

What changes over time

Each action, bill version, fiscal note, referral, hearing notice, companion filing, and author role can add or change signals. The dataset preserves source timestamps and links to the state record.

Who Luna is

Luna is the AI model that reads each bill’s full text. It writes the “In brief” line and the summary, adds topic, agency and search tags, and marks the passages its notes rest on. Everything it writes carries an AI label, can be wrong, and is never official: the bill text and the legislature’s record are. Review progress shows which bills it has read.

Known limitations

Automated agency extraction from captions is incomplete. Predictions in early prefiling are particularly unstable, and committee assignments after the election must be verified before influence scoring.

heading: Save your work.
Keep your watchlist and views on one device, carry them in a link or file, or sync them privately.
about.description: How Texas Bill Atlas saves your watchlist and follows without an account, and how sync links work.
about.html:
NO ACCOUNT NEEDED

Saving and sharing your info

There are no logins on this site. Everything below works without an account, email address or name. Pick whichever fits: keep things on one device, carry them in a link or file, or sync a private link across devices.

Share your watchlist

Both links show only your watched bills. On your watchlist, open Save, share and sync to choose one.

Share a snapshot

When shared
→
After you add a bill

Readers see the bills you picked that day. They can add those bills to their own watchlist.

Star the bills you want to include, then choose Copy share link.

Share a live list

When shared
→
After you add a bill

Readers see your latest list at the same address, including bills you add or remove later.

Choose Create sync link, then Copy view-only link. Keep your edit link private.

Saving on your devices

Your watchlist

Star any bill to follow it. The list is kept in this browser on this device, with nothing sent anywhere. Clearing site data, or using a private window, removes it, so use one of the options below if you want a copy.

Remembered filters

Your last filters and sort order are remembered on this device and come back the next time you visit.

Links to any view

The address bar always describes what you are looking at: the page, filters, sort and any open bill. Use Copy link above the results, or bookmark the page, to return to it or send it to someone.

Export and import a file

Export file saves your watchlist, followed legislators, saved searches and colour theme as one small file you can keep or email. Import file adds them from that file (or an older watchlist export), or from any text or spreadsheet export that mentions bill numbers such as “HB 5” or “SJR 9”. Importing only adds; it never removes bills.

Private sync links

Create sync link on the Watchlist keeps your watchlist, followed legislators, saved searches and colour theme the same on your phone, laptop and work computer, with no account. Light or dark stays a choice for each device. Open the edit link on each device; treat it like a password, because anyone with it can change the list. The view-only link is safe to share: it shows your watchlist’s bills only, never who you follow or what you saved, and stays current as you edit. You can stop syncing one device, or delete the link for every device.

RSS feeds

Each bill’s details include an RSS feed of its recorded actions, for Outlook or any feed reader. A synced watchlist also has one feed for all of its bills, linked from the Watchlist. Each legislator has a feed too, linked from their member page.

Followed legislators

Follow a legislator on their member page or in Near you, and their bills appear under Following. Follows are kept in this browser like the watchlist, and go into exported files and sync links. Share links and view-only links never include them.

Saved searches

On the Bill explorer, Save search keeps the current search words and filters under Following, with how many bills have new actions since you last opened it. Saved searches go into exported files and sync links like follows; share and view-only links never include them.

PRIVACY

What is stored, and where

On this device

  • Watched bills, followed legislators and saved searches
  • Last filters, theme and disclaimer preference
  • Your browser stores your sync link if you made one

On the server

Only when you use a sync link

  • Watched bill numbers, followed member codes and colour theme
  • Saved search names, search words and filters
  • A version number and dates
  • Links only as one-way fingerprints, so the database cannot be used to open a list
Never collectedNames, email addresses, accounts, tracking cookies or analytics
Abuse limitsThe sync service counts requests per address in memory for up to an hour, and never writes addresses down
RetentionA sync link unused for a year is deleted. Deleting it yourself removes it at once; each device keeps its own copy of the list.
Sync on this siteAvailable
This deviceNot synced · 0 bills watched

Limits: up to 500 bills per synced list. Lost your edit link? Your list is still on each device that had it; create a new sync link from any of them.

heading: Behind the tracker.
Understand coverage, refreshes, and how to load or export bill data.
about.description: The sources behind Texas Bill Atlas, how fresh they are, and how to import your own lists.
about.html:
DATA PROVENANCE

Source, coverage & export

Legislative session90R · 2027
Loaded records1384
Snapshot modeofficial-ftp
Read fromLive server snapshot
Last generatedNov 12, 2026, 8:28 AM CT
Luna reviews1,295 reviewed, 1,283 with published tags · updated Nov 12, 2026, 9:41 AM CT
Member roster150 House · 29 Senate · updated Nov 12, 2026, 2:53 AM CT

1384 bill histories read from the official bulk FTP; 1384 combined records. Agency inferences are based on available captions and curated overrides.

Official source policy: The Texas Legislative Council publishes bulk material through anonymous FTP and discourages data mining the public Legislature Online pages. The project includes an updater for the official bulk files, with snapshot validation so a failed import cannot silently replace data with an empty result. Read the source policy ↗
Source code ↗

Imports are temporary to this browser session; they do not alter the public dataset. Watchlist stars are stored on this device.
